newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil firm in Europe, follows Malaysian lead.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil firm in Europe, follows Malaysian lead.

text.p: Palm oil prices firmed on the European vegetable oil market on Wednesday morning following the higher close in Malaysia on talk that Pakistan may have reduced its import duty and concerns over the weather conditions in India.
Traders are awaiting confirmation of any cut in the Pakistani duty.
Reports from India suggest that the El Nino warm water currents could threaten crucial monsoon rains, but meteorological officials and analysts say it is too early to predict the affect.
However, traders in Malaysian jumped on the reports to boost their sagging market.
"Malaysia badly needs to boost its exports of palm oil to stop the decline in prices, so who can blame them for latching on to these reports," said one trader.
In Europe at midday crude palm oil was $2.50 to $5 up after Jul traded at $532.50 and Nov at $527.50 a tonne cif.
Products were around $5 up after RBD palm oil fetched $512.50 a tonne for July and $510 for August.
Olein traded at $552.50 a tonne fob Malaysian ports for July.

Lower Chicago soy oil futures at Tuesday close dragged soft oils in Europe lower with soy oil 0.50 to one guilders down after Aug traded at 103.50 guilders while rape oil was 0.235 guilders below Tuesday's close.
Lauric oils were around $5 up at midday by buyers were lagging $10 behind.
